channel.title: The Seax: Essex news, sport and life
channel.description: The latest Essex news, sport and life, updated through the day.

image.title: The Seax: Essex news, sport and life

item.title: Fyfield field gives up rare 1646 Civil War siege coin
item.description: A detectorist has found a rare Civil War siege coin near Ongar. He fears he may not be allowed to keep it.

item.title: Essex ambulance service rated good after 2025 warning notice
item.description: Inspectors found quicker call handling, more staff and better training. The East of England Ambulance Service answers 999 calls across Essex.

item.title: Southend climb to fourth with 2-0 win at Forest Green
item.description: Southend United won 2-0 at The New Lawn on Tuesday 24 November, bouncing back from their home defeat by leaders Boreham Wood four days earlier.

item.title: Billericay Town hold leaders Ebbsfleet United to a 1-1 draw
item.description: Billericay took a point off the National League South leaders in Kent. An early lead lasted only 10 minutes.

item.title: Maldon Local Plan consultation now open: have your say
item.description: People across Maldon district can say what its next plan for homes and roads should cover. Views close on 22 December.

item.title: Billericay chip pan fire leaves resident with burned hands
item.description: A Billericay resident was hurt in a kitchen fire. Firefighters say never move a burning pan.

item.title: Hanningfield Reservoir hits record low of 35% as hosepipe ban goes on
item.description: Hanningfield, near Chelmsford, is at its lowest level on record. It would normally be about twice as full at this time of year.

item.title: Colchester Local Plan heads to government inspectors
item.description: Colchester's draft Local Plan is to be submitted for independent examination, the Daily Gazette reports.

item.title: Takeley firefighter chisels trapped spaniel's head free from wall
item.description: A two-year-old Springer Spaniel got her head stuck in a decorative cut-out in a Takeley wall. A fire officer freed her with small tools.

item.title: Lower Thames Crossing puts world-first electric haulers to work
item.description: Battery-powered trucks are now moving earth on the route of the new road tunnel between Essex and Kent.

item.title: Loughton's Roding Valley Recreation Ground to get new paths and meadows
item.description: Epping Forest District Council has drawn up a long-term plan to improve Roding Valley Recreation Ground. Developers' money will pay for it.

item.title: Colchester neighbours raise alarm over hob fire in empty house
item.description: Neighbours heard smoke alarms going off in a Colchester house while the resident was out. Firefighters put out a fire on the hob.

item.title: University of Essex students raise safety fears over MoD housing plan
item.description: Some students on the Colchester campus say they feel uneasy about living alongside soldiers. The university says nothing has been decided.

item.title: Maldon house prices up 5% in a year as Tendring's fall 2.2%
item.description: Official September figures show a county split in two. Prices rose in nine Essex areas and fell in five.

item.title: Grays Athletic bring back Darren Manning as director of football
item.description: Grays Athletic have brought back a former manager in a new boardroom role. He left in February with the Thurrock club fighting relegation.

item.title: Cold Norton: police find £300,000 cannabis farm in barn
item.description: Officers found more than 500 plants near Cold Norton after a tip-off. Police say grows like this can be linked to modern slavery.

item.title: Colchester's ROL Cruise named UK's third best company to work for
item.description: A Colchester holiday firm has climbed into the UK's top three workplaces. The ranking is based on what its own staff say.

item.title: Basildon business support scheme ranked in UK's top four for impact
item.description: A Basildon scheme for new and growing firms has won national recognition. It did so on a fraction of its rivals' budgets.

item.title: Hatfield Peverel man, 26, jailed for five years for sexual assaults
item.description: David Cooney is now on the sex offenders' register. The woman he assaulted says she finally has closure.

item.title: Thundersley's Little Havens welcomes back patron Ferne McCann
item.description: TV star Ferne McCann spent an evening with families at Essex's only children's hospice. She is backing its Christmas appeal.

item.title: Rayleigh Lions give £10,000 to school avoidance programme
item.description: The money goes to a programme helping children who struggle to attend school for emotional reasons.

item.title: Hockley volunteers fill 18 bags in community litter pick
item.description: Rochford District Litter Picks met at Clements Hall. Volunteers covered Hockley, Glencrofts and Hawkwell Main Road.

item.title: Epping Forest council crushes fly-tipping truck in a first for the district
item.description: A truck linked to a large fly-tip on Epping Forest heathland has been crushed. It is the council's first use of the power.

item.title: Brightlingsea's first Light Up the Hard asks town to remember loved ones
item.description: Colne Yacht Club invites people to light a candle on 22 December. It is part of Carols on the Hard.

item.title: Chelmsford bus C3 to reach Boreham and Beaulieu Park station in January
item.description: Chelmsford's C3 bus will link Boreham with the new Beaulieu Park station. A Sunday route and an extra hospital shift trip are also coming.

item.title: Epping nurse Tracy Reed honoured for 27 years in community care
item.description: A west Essex nurse has won a national long service award. She joined the NHS as a clerk at 17.

item.title: St Clare Hospice holds seven Light Up a Life services across west Essex
item.description: Anyone can dedicate a star to a loved one, whether or not the hospice cared for them.

item.title: Harlow family centre Savannah Lodge gets new Ofsted notice after visit
item.description: Savannah Lodge in Harlow has improved since Ofsted rated it inadequate in July. One safeguarding notice is still not met.

item.title: Grays' Essex Fire Museum wins Best Museum at Essex Mums Awards
item.description: The free museum at a working Grays fire station beat strong competition, including Essex Police's museum in Chelmsford.

item.title: Ex-England goalkeeper raises £5,642 for Mersea charity
item.description: Peter Shilton has auctioned football keepsakes from his Mersea Island home. The money goes to the gambling charity he runs with his wife.

item.title: Elsenham airport car park told to close by February after appeal fails
item.description: The unauthorised Stansted parking site at New Farm has lost its fight with the council. The land must now be cleared.

item.title: Essex student Moyin Odeniran wins The Great British Bake Off
item.description: The 22-year-old beat Tom Whittaker and Mo Mahir in the Channel 4 final on Tuesday 24 November, with friends and family watching at his local church in Loughton.

item.title: Stansted Airport rehearses plane crash response with 400 people
item.description: The blue lights around the airport on Tuesday 24 November were only a drill. Flights were planned to run as normal.

item.title: Tolleshunt D'Arcy village hall wins £70,000 for January refit
item.description: Tolleshunt D'Arcy's century-old village hall has secured grants for its long-awaited repairs, years after a bid to replace the building outright fell through.

item.title: Thurrock budget cuts face scrutiny, from parking permits to staff phones
item.description: Thurrock Council's draft savings for 2027/28, including dearer permits for second and third cars and an end to buying staff phones, now go before its scrutiny committee.

item.title: Chelmsford City climb into play-offs as Barham penalty beats Maidstone
item.description: Former Stones striker Jack Barham scored for the third time in two days as City edged a tight Monday night game.

item.title: Chelmsford MP backs Paul's Law after Birch care home choking death
item.description: Marie Goldman wants every care worker trained to spot and manage swallowing problems, after a jury found failures in the care of Paul Spearing, who choked on unsuitable food at his care home near Colchester and died in November 2023.

item.title: Chelmsford Chieftains lose 5-3 at Streatham in the Challenge Cup
item.description: Chelmsford's ice hockey side, who won 3-2 at Streatham in the league in October, trailed 3-1 after two periods and could not recover.

item.title: South Essex father jailed for abusing his two vulnerable children
item.description: Detectives showed him video of what he had done, and a judge called it "gratuitous degradation". The children's mother, who delayed telling police, was given a community order.

item.title: Rochford Local Plan must go to inspector by 31 March, minister rules
item.description: Housing minister Matthew Pennycook wants Rochford's housing plan examined within months. He says the district has too little land set aside for homes.

item.title: Army and Navy inquiry opens into £81m Chelmsford junction rebuild
item.description: Up to 75,000 vehicles a day use the Chelmsford junction, which has been over capacity at peak times since its flyover came down in 2019.

item.title: Epping Forest district's 50 favourite trees go on show at museum
item.description: Residents' choice of the 50 best-loved trees in the Epping Forest district is now on display at Epping Forest District Museum, marking 40 years of the council's Countrycare team.

item.title: Thaw Patrol and Snow Be Gone Kenobi join Essex gritting fleet
item.description: Essex's gritters are ready for winter. New lorries with playful names join the fleet that keeps main roads moving in ice and snow.

item.title: Stansted Airport links 140+ local firms to its terminal expansion work
item.description: Local businesses met buyers at London Stansted's 25th Meet the Buyers event, as the airport looks for suppliers for its five-year terminal transformation.

item.title: Basildon Hospital gas and air halt 'completely unacceptable', says midwife union
item.description: The RCM says Basildon Hospital has had years to make gas and air safe for staff. Women in labour are offered alternative pain relief.

item.title: Grays drug-driver jailed over death of man, 72, hit by reversing van
item.description: Billy Howard-Smith, 26, has been sentenced to 40 months in prison for causing the death of Roy Hibbert in Lodge Lane, Grays.

item.title: Colchester Borough Homes wins top MoD award for Armed Forces support
item.description: Colchester's council housing company has been given the Gold Award under the Defence Employer Recognition Scheme, the Ministry of Defence's highest honour for employers.

item.title: Chelmsford rough sleeping rose 50% in four years, council says
item.description: Chelmsford City Council's rough sleeping navigators help people off the streets and into housing. They say more people are sleeping rough in the city each year, though the rise is slower than across England.

item.title: Southend Victoria line trains replaced by buses on 28 and 29 November
item.description: Rail passengers from Southend, Wickford and the Crouch Valley face a weekend of replacement buses as Network Rail carries out maintenance on the Southend Victoria and Southminster lines.

item.title: Chelmsford City captain Cav Miley falls down badger hole in training
item.description: Manager Mark Cooper said the fall affected Miley's game as the Clarets let a two-goal lead slip at Walton & Hersham.

item.title: Brentwood and Rochford invite businesses to become Safe Spaces for women
item.description: Both councils are holding drop-in events through the 16 Days of Activism against gender-based violence to recruit businesses and community groups to the Women's Safety Charter.

item.title: Harlow Council on track for fourth budget surplus in a row
item.description: The council has kept its share of council tax frozen since 2021, and says its credit rating has been upgraded to AA−.

item.title: Southend Airport hunts first Chief Christmas Officer with Lapland prize
item.description: London Southend Airport is looking for its first Chief Christmas Officer, and the winner and a guest fly to Lapland for the day on 22 December.

item.title: HARP appeals for pre-loved prom dresses for south Essex teenagers
item.description: Homelessness charity HARP is asking for donated prom dresses and free hair and beauty services so young people across south Essex can afford to go to their prom.

item.title: Greater Anglia and c2c target under-16s as crossing misuse rises 65%
item.description: A crossing near Upminster has been shut for almost eight weeks after children were filmed doing handstands and playing chicken with trains.

item.title: Remus Horse Sanctuary asks for help with £5,400 a month hay bill
item.description: Remus Horse Sanctuary near Ingatestone is asking supporters to back its hay appeal on GivingTuesday, Tuesday 1 December, as feed costs climb.

item.title: Harlow hospital gets coroner warning over resuscitation decisions
item.description: A coroner's report says staff at the Princess Alexandra Hospital do not fully understand the rules on do not resuscitate decisions. The hospital has replied, setting out the changes it is making.

item.title: QEII bridge reopens after police incident adds to a torrid day at Dartford
item.description: Everything was open again by 6.20pm, but drivers going both ways faced hours of queues, and more overnight closures follow this week.

item.title: Braintree cat Zeus takes 37-mile solo train trip to Liverpool Street
item.description: A Braintree cat got on an evening train by himself. Station staff in London spotted him and sent him home.

item.title: Wickford derailment repairs to cost Network Rail £3.65m
item.description: The bill covers the repairs after a Greater Anglia train came off the rails south of Wickford during August's heatwave. Investigators are still working out why it happened.
